questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: McGill as a school, and I have always wanted to see some part of Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Sufficiently easy and nice people at the exchange student office who were very helpful and understanding.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Online guidance, preparation and welcome online seminars, email information and in-person assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I looked at the housing sites recommended by McGill, and wrote to a few places. No real recommendations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked it and I heard others enjoyed living off campus too. It was till very close to campus, so literally two streets away from the on-campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All online through their student system. No flexibility. What's not doable in the system is not doable at all.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Exchange student administrators and professors, but no one could do anything outside of the online system. But they helped with guidance and explanations.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. But I fortunately got into other very interesting and relevant ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that McGill does not allow or open for exchange students in all courses. Depending on your degree this may be more or less applicable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All courses were Master's courses besides one. However, some of the MA courses had been rearranged or opened to BA, so while the content was previously Master's level now it was part of the BA programme.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Small seminars, more individual work and intermediate reporting. However, also some group presentations and papers.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EDPE 561 Machine Learning: Thry & Apps
ENVB 530 Adv GIS for Natural Res Mgmt
INSY 448 Text & Social Media Analytics
ORGB 421 Managing Organizational Change
POLI 312 Intermed. Quant. Political Sci

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Machine Learning: Thry & Apps : Amazing professor, great hands-on work possibility, creating your own machine learning algorithm and application.

Text & Social Media Analytics: Highly knowledgable professor.

Adv GIS for Natural Res Mgmt: Very interesting and hands-on for anyone interested in working with satellite imagery and tools like ArcGIS or QGIS.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee shops and restaurants less expensive than in Copenhagen. Same for housing. Food from grocery stores possibly on the same level.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many, from football to swimming to book, theater, debate or other clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The events and trips organised for exchange students by the abroad office.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Ottawa and Quebec City as well as Toronto.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Perfectly fine, not challenging.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There is a mentor programme one can sign up for who could then possibly connect you further.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very multi-cultural, chatty and open.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be flexible around courses. Be prepared for a busy and full workload throughout the entire semester. Be aware attendance and participation count towards your final grade.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are lots of academic and professional networking events organised across various facilities. Not all are open for exchange students, unfortunately, but make sure to subscribe to various newsletters from different faculties not only your own.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The content and work in the courses and studies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not being able to work part-time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
